source: NCERT Class XI, Themes in World History, Ch. 5 (Changing Cultural Traditions).

sections.heading: 1. The Renaissance — Meaning and Setting
points: The chapter covers **changing cultural traditions in Europe, c. 1300–1800**, centred on the **Renaissance** ('rebirth').
It began in the towns of **Italy** (especially **Florence, Venice, Rome**) and spread across Europe.
It was marked by a **revival of interest in classical Greek and Roman learning, art and ideas**.

sections.heading: 2. Humanism
points: **Humanism** — a new way of thinking that stressed **human beings, reason, and this-worldly life** rather than only religion.
Humanists studied grammar, rhetoric, poetry, history and philosophy (the 'humanities').
It encouraged **individualism, curiosity and a questioning spirit**; the human being was seen as capable and dignified.

sections.heading: 3. Art, Science and Realism
points: Renaissance **art** achieved realism using **anatomy, geometry and perspective**; artists were also scientists.
Great figures: **Leonardo da Vinci** (Mona Lisa, The Last Supper), **Michelangelo** (Sistine Chapel, David), **Raphael**.
**Science** advanced: **Copernicus** (heliocentric theory — the Sun, not the Earth, at the centre), later **Galileo, Kepler, Newton** — the **Scientific Revolution**.
The **printing press (Gutenberg)** spread new ideas rapidly.

sections.heading: 4. Religion, Reformation and Wider World
points: The **Reformation** — **Martin Luther** (1517) challenged the Catholic Church; **Protestantism** arose; the Church responded (Counter-Reformation).
New ideas of the **state, citizenship and the individual** developed.
European voyages and contact with other continents widened horizons; a distinct sense of **European identity** and modern outlook took shape.
The debate on whether it was truly a sudden 'rebirth' or a gradual change is part of the theme.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Renaissance = 'rebirth'; began in Italian towns (Florence, Venice, Rome).
Humanism = focus on human beings, reason, this-worldly life.
Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Raphael = Renaissance artists.
Copernicus = heliocentric theory (Sun at centre); start of Scientific Revolution.
Reformation = Martin Luther (1517) → Protestantism; printing press spread ideas.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The Renaissance **began in Italy** (Florence).
**Humanism** stressed **human reason and this-worldly life** (not rejection of religion, but a shift of emphasis).
**Copernicus** proposed the **heliocentric (Sun-centred)** theory.
**Martin Luther (1517)** began the **Reformation** → Protestantism.
